newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower on correction.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower on correction.

text.p: Stocks closed lower on Saturday on profit-taking after recent sharp climbs, brokers said.
The composite stock index stood at 693.14 at the close of the half day's trading, down 7.73 points or 1.10 percent.
"Stocks ended lower on profit-taking after hopes of pension funds buying boosted share prices higher this week," said Choo Hee-yeop of Daewoo Securities.
Brokers said pension funds were not seen actively buying in the market on Saturday.
"Because of the Christmas holiday, next week will a quiet market," Choo said.
Profit taking was focused on large-cap shares. Daewoo Heavy Industries fell 200 won to 5,400 won and Samsung Corp lost 400 won to 10,100 won.

There was some buying in individual shares. Sammi Steel rose 200 won to 4,490 won. It plans to sell parts of its stainless steel business to POSCO. Samsung Display Devices was the most active stock of the day. It climbed 1,300 won to 50600 won.
Volume totalled 21.5 million shares on Saturday. Losers beat gainers 507 to 352.
